title: EPIGENETICS phase-length sweep: phase-1 attractor lock is permanent across T2 in {10,50,100,500}
question: Does a longer phase-2 (rule30) eventually escape the phase-1 (rule110) attractor that H_332 found dominant?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=4 ECA. T1=10 rule110, then T2 rule30 sweep. Manhattan distance of final-state histogram to rule110-only and rule30-only baselines.

falsifier_eval.F335_1_LOCK_PERSISTS: PASS — d(hybrid, rule110-baseline) = 0.0 at EVERY T2 including 500; the hybrid never drifts from the rule110 attractor
falsifier_eval.F335_2_NO_ESCAPE_TO_PHASE2: PASS — d(hybrid, rule30-baseline) stays 1.25 at every T2; phase-2 never reshapes the distribution toward its own attractor
falsifier_eval.F335_3_FLAT_ACROSS_T2: PASS — both distances are constant across a 50× range of T2 (10→500), indicating the lock is exact, not asymptotic

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — phase-1 attractor lock is PERMANENT. Even at T2=500 (50× the phase-1 length), the hybrid final-state distribution is byte-identical to the rule110-only baseline (d=0.0) and maximally far from the rule30-only baseline (d=1.25). Mechanistically this means rule110's attractor set is CLOSED under rule30 dynamics — once the system enters the rule110 attractor during phase 1, the rule30 update map permutes those states within the same set and can never carry the system out. This is a strong, exact epigenetic-memory result: the phase-1 history is permanently inherited regardless of phase-2 duration.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel (2-phase forward orbit). The discovery is cross-rule attractor invariance: rule110's attractor is a closed set under rule30, so the epigenetic lock is not asymptotic decay but exact permanence.
honest_limits: n=4; at larger n the rule110 attractor may not stay closed under rule30 (the n=8 oscillation H_334 suggests attractor structure is n-dependent)
Single rule pair (110 then 30); the reverse order and other pairs may not lock — H_332 reverse (30 then 110) also locked to rule110, but a full pair sweep is open
Manhattan distance on the final-state marginal; a trajectory-level metric might reveal transient excursions that the marginal hides
T2 capped at 500; though flatness across 10→500 makes asymptotic escape implausible, it is not a proof for all T2
discovery_note: epigenetic lock이 asymptotic decay가 아니라 EXACT permanence. rule110 attractor set이 rule30 dynamics 하에서 closed (invariant). 이는 H_332 attractor-dominance를 'cross-rule attractor invariance' 메커니즘으로 정밀화.
